data.headline: Video from your own code
data.kicker: A lesson and a brand go in. A narrated video comes out.

beats.say: Kinetry is a video engine you call from your own code.
Give it a lesson and a brand, and you get back a narrated video in that brand.

data.headline: Install it once
data.title: terminal
data.note: Setup fetches the pinned renderer and browser.

beats.say: Install the package, with the model providers and the free local voice.
Then run setup. It fetches a pinned renderer and browser, so every render looks the same.

data.headline: Four calls in Python
data.title: make_video.py
data.note: The plan is plain data: review or edit it before you render.

beats.say: In Python, pick any model with your own key. Then read the brand from a website, and plan the video from your lesson.
The plan is plain data, so you can review or edit it. Then render.

data.headline: Or call the service
data.title: terminal
data.note: Poll the job, or get a signed callback when it's done.

beats.say: From any other language, run it as a service, and post a plan to the videos endpoint.
Then poll the job, or get a signed callback when the video is ready.
The same engine comes as a Python library, an HTTP service, and an MCP server for agents.
There are LangChain tools, a Docker image, and a command line too.

data.label: to $0.11 in model calls for 90 seconds of video
data.sub: With Claude Sonnet on Bedrock and the free local voice. It renders on your own servers.

beats.say: A ninety-second video costs about six to eleven cents in model calls.
That's with Claude Sonnet on Bedrock and the free local voice, rendered on your own servers.

data.headline: Make your first video
data.meta: Everything is in the docs: kinetry.xyz/docs

beats.say: Everything is in the docs. Make your first video today.
